technical_and_design_decisions: Refactor existing reactor-based gpfdist code from spring-xd-modules to remove XD-specific dependencies and align with Spring Framework 6.0 Java 17+ requirements
Implement a GitHub REST API-backed module registry adapter with local metadata caching to reduce API call overhead, supporting GitHub personal access token authentication for write operations
Use existing Spring XD container benchmarking tooling for RabbitMQ performance testing, with isolated Rackspace cloud test environments to avoid external interference
Extend the existing Flo data model to include structured error fields (error code, detailed message, remediation steps) without breaking backward compatibility for existing API clients
Reuse the existing Java Mail library dependency in the Mail source module, mapping the java-mail-properties attribute directly to the Java Mail Properties object without additional transformation
Implement HDFS as the default module registry with a fallback to local file system for development environments, using existing HDFS client libraries already included in the project dependencies

Parse the xd-shell.init file as a sequence of standard xd-shell commands, executing them in order after shell startup, with error logging for invalid commands but continued execution of remaining valid commands

Implement graceful stream shutdown as an opt-in configuration option to avoid breaking existing stream deployment behavior, with a configurable timeout for waiting for in-flight message processing before forced shutdown
assumptions: Full access to the spring-xd-modules repository, GitHub API (with appropriate permissions for the centralized registry repository), Rackspace cloud environment, test GPDB/HAWQ instances, and test HDFS cluster is available for development and testing
Existing Spring XD and Spring Framework codebases are accessible, up to date with Spring 6.0 Java 17+ requirements, and do not require major architectural changes to support the specified features

All required test environments (unit, integration, performance) are pre-configured and available for use, with no additional environment setup effort required beyond what is listed in the activity breakdown
Standard load testing tools (e.g., JMeter, Gatling) already available in the project are sufficient for RabbitMQ benchmarking, with no new tooling development required
The Java Mail library version already used by the Mail source module supports all required SSL/TLS properties for IMAP/SMTP, with no library upgrade needed
The HDFS cluster used for the module registry is compatible with the existing HDFS client libraries in the project, with no client library changes required
The existing stream deployment and undeployment logic can be extended to support graceful shutdown without requiring a full rewrite of the stream lifecycle management code
